posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
No. You can use event commands to react to the player pushing buttons.
There should be lots of tutorials for this kind of thing floating around - in fact, I know I've seen someone specifically reference a tutorial for creating a book with pages exactly like this.
But here's one for how to make an evented menu, generally.
Eventing a Picture-Based Menu | The Official RPG Maker Blog
The default RPG Maker menu works well, but sometimes you want one that fits your game’s aesthetic better or offers only the important options. Eventing your own picture-based menu is a great way to make sure your menu fits your game, so let’s take a look at how to make one.
www.rpgmakerweb.com

posts.author: TheAM-Dol
posts.body:
Following the tutorial is best.
But in summary, what you would do is:
Create a common event that you can attach to your "scrap book" item.
Activating this item will do a show picture.
The common event will be an autorun event monitoring for player input.
(isTriggered is going to be the ideal one, isPressed will likely make pages flip uncontrollably. <-advanced information)
If the game progresses linearly, then simply increase a variable, "GameProgress" by 1. GameProgress+1 each time a major story event completes.
In the common event you'd use a conditional to display the pictures based on the GameProgress variable.
As a bonus, you could just use a white image, roughly the size of the scrap book, and shrink the width of the white image to reveal more pictures.
Anyways, this is definitely something that can be evented with a little bit of learning and a little bit of trial-and-error, so I definitely encourage you to go the evented route, rather than relying on a plugin for this one.
